claims: NASA's Artemis II mission successfully launched on April 1, 2026, from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
NASA's Artemis II mission marks the first crewed flight to the Moon in over 50 years.
NASA's Artemis II mission has a duration of approximately 10 days.
NASA's Artemis II mission features a four-person crew consisting of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The crew of NASA's Artemis II mission is testing the Orion spacecraft and its life-support systems in deep space.
The crew of NASA's Artemis II mission consists of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency (CSA) astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
NASA's Artemis II mission involves launching into Earth orbit.
NASA's Artemis II mission involves performing a manual test-drive of the Orion capsule.
NASA's Artemis II mission involves traveling around the far side of the Moon before returning to Earth.

The purpose of NASA's Artemis II mission is to demonstrate that the Orion spacecraft's systems—including life support, navigation, and propulsion—are safe for human spaceflight before future lunar landing missions.
NASA's Artemis II mission includes a "perigee raise burn" on April 2, 2026.
The "perigee raise burn" of NASA's Artemis II mission is to shape the orbit for the translunar journey.
